text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT triggered: runtime OOM on prod-cluster-4 (sev3). Symptoms: elevated OOM rate on runtime workers serving /v1/generate, increased paging on GPU 2/4. Pager: @ryan oncall. Incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1709004321
ryan: ack — I'm looking. Can folks drop immediate telemetry (nvidia-smi + dmesg + runtime logs) and any recent deploy info? I'll start triage and escalate if needed.
jess: I'm standing by for logs. Observed a small spike in KV cache growth 10:13–10:16 UTC before the first OOM alerts.
maria: copying recent deploys — no model or runtime deploys in last 2 hours. Autoscaler events show a couple of node reboots at ~10:05 but unrelated? linking infra events: https://infra.redwood/reboots/1709004200
support-bot: customer-impact estimate: ~4 customers (high-volume) showing 3–8% error rate on generate calls, 2 started reporting timeouts. No broad outage yet.
ryan: ok. jess, can you paste GPU memory traces and a quick histogram of tensor sizes? Also want per-request batch sizes around the time window.
jess: past 15m nvidia-smi snapshot (summarized):
```
GPU0  24%  used 6.1GiB / 48GiB
GPU1  40%  used 19.8GiB / 48GiB
GPU2  96%  used 46.2GiB / 48GiB  <-- paging thrash
GPU3  30%  used 14.0GiB / 48GiB
```
Runtime logs show repeated GC-like free attempts and hyperpage faults. Stack snippet (trimmed):
```
OOM at runtime::alloc_tensor_batch (batch_size=8, seq_len=2048) -> fallback to host swap
kv_cache: growth delta +1.2GiB/10m
```
maria: batch-size distribution near window: p95 batch_size=8, p50=4. A/B routing shows spike of large-batch low-latency customers routed to cluster-4 around 10:12.
tim: hypothesis 1: KV cache growth + a sudden influx of large sequences caused fragmentation on GPU2 leading to paging and OOM.
hypothesis 2: a background maintenance job pinned memory and reduced available slabs causing allocation failures (infra reboot logs?)
ryan: trying a quick mitigation: reduce max_batch_size at routing layer for cluster-4 from 8 -> 4 and enable aggressive KV eviction for 10m. Pushing config now.
ryan: pushed. Monitor please.
lina: logs show drop in OOM alerts within 70s of the change. Paging counters on GPU2 decreased from 120 faults/min -> 18 faults/min.
support-bot: customer-impact update: errors dropped back to baseline for 3/4 affected customers, the remaining customer on long sequences still had intermittent timeouts.
jess: digging in kernel logs — saw nv_peer_memory page reclaim spikes. Also found contiguous allocation failures preceding OOM: suggests fragmentation not just absolute usage.
tim: actionable: try lowering prefetch KV window and force defragmentation cycle on next maintenance window. Also consider enabling model quantization variant for that noisy tenant as a short-term mitigation.
maria: started talk with sales/AM to notify the affected customer and offer rate-limited fallback. Ticket #TICK-4823 created.
ryan: documenting timeline in the incident doc and collecting logs: pulled runtime dump, KV cache growth logs, and per-request batch traces at /tmp/inc-1709004321.tar.gz (shared to secure-logs channel).
jess: adding quick commands we ran for telemetry for record:
```
kubectl logs -l app=runtime -n prod --since=30m | grep -E "OOM|kv_cache|page_fault"
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 1
cat /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 500 | grep -E "Nv|oom|page_fault"
```
ryan: follow-ups: 1) postmortem with timeline + root cause hypothesis (KV fragmentation + large-batch spike) 2) implement routing guard for large batch dispatch to clusters with >80% fragment risk 3) add proactive defrag/compact in runtime 4) customer outreach notes (lina)
maria: assigning owners: defrag work -> tim, routing guard -> ryan, postmortem writeup -> jess, customer comms -> lina. ETA for playbook PRs: 72h.
support-bot: incident severity downgraded to sev4 at 10:26 UTC. Still under monitoring.
ryan: thanks all. Saving logs and closing the live triage. We'll reconvene in the RCA doc and stitch a clear timeline and evidence attachments. :thumbsup:
